ratings.note: Colour-blind volunteers are on every rota (occasional); in the deuteranopia capture the red float dot matches the green ones, so they cannot identify the faulty sensor (blocks task 3); static, cannot be learned around. s=4.
Forced-colours capture shows an empty Status column: for those users no status exists at all (blocks task 3); forced-colours use is not declared among users, so rare; never overcome. s=4.

Forced-colours capture shows only the label, no switch; the status sentence still states the mode, so significant difficulty locating the control rather than a block; rare population; recurs each visit. s=3.

Probe after-reload screenshot shows switch on and 'automatic' after the grower set manual; shared tablet is reloaded/viewed by others at each reservoir change (common); safety setting misreported, risk of dosing an empty tank; cannot be learned around. s=4.
ARIA tree shows all five status cells empty; the screen-reader volunteer cannot learn any sensor status (blocks task 3); one known user, so rare; no workaround on the page. s=4.

Two of five sensors are amber/red in shipped data and hover reveals nothing (common); novice must find someone to interpret (significant difficulty); meaning can be learned over time, so overcome once learned. s=3.

Screenshot shows green 'Topped up 09:30' beside a red Reservoir float dot; arises only while the float faults (occasional); may lead a volunteer to drain/act on a wrong belief (significant error); learnable once the lead explains. s=3.

Cards show verdicts but no range on every view (nearly always); verdict text already answers 'in range?' for 3 of 4 and the shift checklist covers ranges, so a minor delay mainly for 'Warm'; learned over shifts. s=3; rated 2 because the verdicts carry most of what task 2 needs.

Screenshots show a line with time labels only; the current pH card already gives 'In range', so trend reading is a secondary need (common); misreading a dip is an annoyance more than an error; recurs but users learn to ignore the chart. s=2.

ARIA shows Conductivity / EC probe / EC 1.8 and similar pairs; met by novices and visitors linking readings to sensors (common); names are close enough to map with a moment's thought (minor); learned once. s=2.

Probe shows one click restores automatic with no dialog; an accidental tap during reservoir work is rare but would dose an empty tank (equipment/money loss); the status sentence does change, so attentive users notice. s=3.

Absence check and manual-state screenshots show only the switch and history; met every manual session (common); user must learn elsewhere that pumps are started at the controller (minor detour); learned once. s=2.
